source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Two things about power board which I think is final:
1\. Physical power button connector — a 2-pin JST-GH connector (J\_PWR\_BTN) for a panel-mounted momentary button wired to the AXP2101 PWRON pin. Press to turn on, press to turn off.
2\. DCDC1 output voltage — set AXP2101 DCDC1 to 3.4V (not 3.3V) via I2C to compensate for the Schottky diode drop on the main board power OR-ing circuit, keeping the 3.3V rail at the correct voltage under all conditions.

value_updates.source_selection: Schottky-diode OR-ing selects the available source; AXP2101 DCDC1 is programmed to 3.4V before the diode so the system rail remains at 3.3V.
value_updates.normal_operation_source: AXP2101 DCDC1 programmed to 3.4V via I2C before the main-board Schottky OR-ing drop

decisions.reason: The same message independently introduces the panel power-button connector, but the DCDC1 voltage change does not alter that connector or its control behavior.
The source changes the AXP2101 DCDC1 output feeding the 3.3V path, not the MT3608 5V boost converter, its enable control, or its loads.
AXP2101 remains the normal-operation source for all system loads, and the battery input range and overall power-path roles remain unchanged.
The DCDC1 voltage compensation does not change the charge-status display, CHGLED connector, resistor values, or population requirements.
The source does not change battery overcharge, overdischarge, short-circuit, or DW01A protection behavior.
The DCDC1 output setting does not alter the battery NTC connection or AXP2101 thermal-protection behavior.
The power-board input to the main board is no longer accurately described as an incoming 3.3V source: DCDC1 now supplies 3.4V before the main-board Schottky drop.
